objective: Exact computation on random connected cubic glues of 8 to 10 lines with a class without solutions: for every line and every class of the glue without it, whether one row of creation tells the classes that tie the removed line's points from the others; where it fails, against two-vertex cuts of the incidence graph; whether the K4^(3) far side stays silent at lines meeting the removed line once under the tie, there and on the trisum glues; and the local lemma that no single near point makes K4^(3) create.
status: Proved (computed): on random cubic glues one row reads the removed line's tie exactly away from two-vertex cuts, and on every 3-connected glue tested; K4^(3)'s silence under the tie fails on a 12-line trisum glue; no single near point makes K4^(3) create
title: Where one row reads the removed line's tie
